scope: Theorem 3.3 (Contour limits) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ϱ = b 1 − b = − cos (︄ πγ2 4 )︄ , γ ∈ ( √ 2, 2), κ = 16 γ2 . The diffusively rescaled bilateral resolved contours converge, uniformly on compact time intervals in law, to a bilateral Brownian motion whose marginal variance rates are one and whose correlation is ϱ. For a length-2n word conditioned to reduce to the empty word, the same rescaling, with duration one, converges uniformly in law to the corresponding quadrant Brownian excursion from (0, 0) to (0, 0). For an unconditioned raw block of O(n) letters, the number of flexible orders left unidentified by reduction of the block is oP( √ n). Consequently changing their resolutions changes the rescaled contour increments by oP(1) uniformly on that block.
